description: The TIMESTAMP_LTZ / TIMESTAMP_NTZ / TIMESTAMP_TZ types with precision. The DESCRIBE TABLE type cell names the subtype, and the declared fractional-second precision is read from INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS.DATETIME_PRECISION (default 9, and 0 through 9 accepted). Also covers a TIMESTAMP_LTZ DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP column filling itself on insert, the refusal of that default on a narrowed precision (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP carries the maximum fractional-second precision, so TIMESTAMP_LTZ(3) cannot take it while TIMESTAMP_LTZ(9) can), a NULL insert round-trip, and plain TIMESTAMP still working. Converted 1:1 from features/TimestampLtzTest (now retired). The Java class read precision off the metastore model behind an embedded-only assume because the DESCRIBE type cell does not spell type parameters; the converted suite reads it through INFORMATION_SCHEMA instead, so the precision claims now run on every backend.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE test_ts_ltz (id INTEGER, ts TIMESTAMP_LTZ)
DESCRIBE TABLE test_ts_ltz
SELECT STARTSWITH("type", 'TIMESTAMP_LTZ') FROM TABLE(RESULT_SCAN(LAST_QUERY_ID())) WHERE "name" = 'TS'
SELECT DATA_TYPE, DATETIME_PRECISION FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS WHERE TABLE_NAME = 'TEST_TS_LTZ' AND COLUMN_NAME = 'TS'
